# Recommended laboratory assessments of exposed persons prior to providing nPEP:

# A) Baseline labs:

Labs: Comprehensive Metabolic AND CBC with Diff

*Local guidance (Des Moines CDSS, Inpatient):*
Order HIV Rapid Test to assess status for all persons:
Next steps in assessment depends on if Rapid HIV test is positive or negative.
Labs: HIV Rapid Test (results in ~60 minutes)
NEGATIVE Rapid HIV Test:
IF Rapid HIV Test is NEGATIVE, continue with assessment for nPEP.
POSITIVE Rapid HIV Test:
IF Rapid HIV Test is POSITIVE, order a confirmatory HIV test.
Patients with baseline rapid tests indicating existing HIV infection should NOT be started on nPEP.
Next steps in assessment depends on if Confirmatory HIV test is positive or negative.
Labs: HIV Ag/Ab confirmatory test (results ~4hours)
NEGATIVE Confirmatory HIV Test:
IF Confirmatory HIV Test is NEGATIVE, continue with assessment for nPEP.
POSITIVE Confirmatory HIV Test:
IF Confirmatory HIV Test is POSITIVE, consult ID. Do not start nPEP.
PAGE the INPATIENT ID Attending for HIV Positive Patients CDC Guidelines 2016

---

# B) HIV Testing

# Order HIV Ag/Ab to assess status for all persons:

Lab: HIV Ag/Ab

Note:  Negative result reported in approximately 1 hour Preliminary positive result sent out to Quest for confirmation (may take 3-5 days for confirmation)

# Next steps in assessment depends on if HIV Ag/Ab result is positive or negative:

# NEGATIVE HIV Ag/Ab Test:

IF HIV Ag/Ab result is NEGATIVE, continue with assessment for nPEP.

# POSITIVE HIV Ag/Ab Test:

IF HIV Ag/Ab inhouse preliminary result is POSITIVE, this may indicate pre-existing HIV infection (pending confirmation from send out lab).

Please PAGE INPATIENT INFECTIOUS DISEASE on all such patients.

Mpls ON-CALL Schedule

---

# C) Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C labs to assess status:

Labs: Hepatitis B Serology and Hepatitis C Antibody

Consult Gastroenterology Liver Outpatient for Hep B or Hep C Positive patients

# D) For females of child-bearing years:

Labs: Pregnancy Screen

For women of reproductive capacity who have had genital exposure to semen and a negative pregnancy test when evaluated for possible nPEP, current contraception use should be assessed, and if a risk for pregnancy exists, emergency contraception should be discussed with the patient.

# E) For all persons considered for or prescribed nPEP for sexual exposure:

Labs: Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, and Syphilis

# **ADD Labs** below for relevant exposure:

Call Lab x2400 for APTIMA Unisex Swab Specimen Collection Kit
Lab: Throat  swab for Chlamydia with Gonorrhea (submit only ONE swab in media)

Lab: Rectal  swab for Chlamydia with Gonorrhea (submit only ONE swab in media)

Lab: Vaginal swab for Chlamydia with Gonorrhea (submit only ONE swab in media)
